title: Where does a line of hieroglyphs begin?
steps: Choose one caption group rather than the entire wall.
Find a human, bird or animal sign with a clear facing direction. The start is normally on the side it faces.
Read into the faces, not in the direction the creatures appear to travel.
Check which depicted figure the caption belongs to; captions can be oriented with their figures.
Identify vertical arrangement separately; facing alone does not tell you how every sign group is ordered.

claims.text: Signs normally face the beginning of a line, and captions align with their associated figures.

limits: This teaches orientation, not a translation. A Karnak sign-by-sign example still needs an edition-matched image.
Ordinary conventions have exceptions; avoid applying this as an automatic decoding algorithm.
